1.title: The name Samuel
1.text: The name 'Samuel' recalls that Hannah 'asked him of the Lord.' She dedicated him to God's service in keeping with the vow she made at the temple.

1.question: Why was Hannah in anguish at the start of the book?
options: She was barren and provoked by Peninnah
She had been rejected by Elkanah, her husband
She had lost all of her family's inheritance
She had been abandoned by her own father

1.question: What did the priest Eli think when he saw Hannah praying silently in the temple?
options: That she was drunk
That she was a prophetess
That she was stealing
That she was a foreigner

1.question: What vow did Hannah make to the Lord?
options: To dedicate her son to the Lord all the days of his life
To offer a hundred lambs to the Lord as a perpetual sacrifice
To never again provoke her rival Peninnah for the rest of her life
To consecrate all her wealth to the sanctuary

1.question: What name did Hannah give her son, recalling that she asked him of the Lord?
options: Samuel
Saul
David
Eli

1.question: When did Hannah bring the boy to the temple at Shiloh?
options: After she had weaned him
On the day he was born
At age twelve
She never brought him

1.question: What did Hannah do with Samuel at the temple of Shiloh?
options: She gave him to the Lord, into Eli's care
She took him back to her own home in Ramah
She left him with the corrupt sons of Eli
She presented him to rival priests

2.title: Hannah's song
2.text: Hannah's song, praising the God who 'raiseth up the poor out of the dust,' inspires Mary's Magnificat in the Gospel of Luke.

2.question: What is Hannah's prayer at the start of chapter 2?
options: A song of praise to the Lord
An accusation against the corrupt priests
A request for pardon for the people's sins
A complaint against the priest

2.question: What theme marks Hannah's song?
options: God brings low the proud and lifts up the humble
The strength of armies guarantees victory over enemies
The wealth of the powerful secures their hold on power
Priests must increase the offerings of the people

2.question: What were Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli, like?
options: Corrupt priests who knew not the Lord
Faithful priests who always served the Lord with zeal
Brave warriors who always defended the nation of Israel
Levites devoted to the service of the temple

2.question: What was the sin of Eli's sons at the sanctuary?
options: They despised the offerings and abused the people
They refused to pray before the altar of the Lord
They worshiped idols brought from foreign lands
They completely abandoned the sacred temple

2.question: What did the Lord do for Hannah after she dedicated Samuel?
options: He gave her more children
He made her queen
He took her to Shiloh
He healed her husband

2.question: How did the boy Samuel grow before the Lord and men?
options: In stature and in favor
In wealth and great fame
In military power and conquests
In complete isolation

2.question: What did the man of God announce to Eli?
options: That his house would be judged for his sons' sin
That he would be crowned king over all the people of Israel
That he would live for many long years in complete peace
That he would rebuild the temple at Shiloh

2.question: What did God promise to raise up in place of Eli's house?
options: A faithful priest
A new great prophet
A large new army force
A brand new city

3.title: The word was rare
3.text: 'The word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision.' Samuel's call marks the return of the prophetic voice to Israel.

3.question: When the Lord called the boy Samuel at night, what did he think at first?
options: That it was Eli calling
That it was the voice of an angel
That it was another boy calling
That it was the wind in the tent

3.question: What did Eli teach Samuel to answer the Lord?
options: 'Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth'
'Go to the altar and bow before the Lord'
'Ask him what thy name shall be, O Lord'
'Say nothing, only listen in silence'

3.question: What message did the Lord give Samuel that night?
options: The judgment on Eli's house
The restoration of the priesthood in Israel
The coming victory over the Philistines
The choosing of a new priest

3.question: How did all Israel come to recognize Samuel?
options: As a faithful prophet of the Lord
As a judge appointed over all Israel
As a trusted counselor to King Saul
As a keeper of the temple records

4.title: I-chabod: 'the glory is departed'
4.text: On hearing the ark was taken, Eli's daughter-in-law gave birth and named the child I-chabod, saying, 'The glory is departed from Israel.'

4.question: What did Israel take into battle, thinking it would defeat the Philistines?
options: The ark of the covenant
The tablets of the law of Moses
The whole tabernacle
The priestly garments

4.question: What happened in the battle where the ark was taken?
options: The ark was captured and Eli's sons died
Israel defeated the Philistines and reclaimed the land
The Philistines withdrew and returned the ark in peace
Eli was captured, but his sons escaped

4.question: Who brought Eli the news of the defeat?
options: A man of Benjamin who fled the battle
A Philistine messenger sent with the news
One of Eli's sons, who survived the attack
A young priest coming from Shiloh

4.question: What happened to Eli when he heard the ark was taken?
options: He fell off his seat and died
He tore his clothes and wept bitterly
He ran to the battlefield
He remained silent and prayed

5.title: Dagon, the Philistine idol
5.text: Dagon was the chief god of the Philistines. Before the ark of the Lord his image fell to the ground and broke — showing who the true God is.

5.question: What happened to the idol Dagon before the ark of the Lord?
options: It fell to the ground and broke
It remained standing without moving
It was covered with a dark veil
It was taken far away from there

5.question: What afflicted the Philistines while they kept the ark?
options: They were struck with tumors
They were attacked by swarms of locusts
They suffered intense hunger and thirst
They lost their harvests

5.question: What did the Philistines finally decide to do with the ark?
options: Send it back to Israel
Burn it
Hide it in the sea
Sell it to Egypt

6.title: The gold offering
6.text: The Philistines sent with the ark an offering of golden tumors and mice — acknowledging the plague had come from the hand of the God of Israel.

6.question: How did the Philistines return the ark to Israel?
options: On a new cart, with an offering of gold
Carried by priests to the temple of Dagon
On a silver litter, escorted by the princes
Hidden in a cave in the mountains

6.question: What sign would show whether the plague had truly come from the God of Israel?
options: The cows going straight to Beth-shemesh, not turning aside
The cows returning alone to the far land of the Philistines
Fire falling from heaven upon the priests of Dagon's temple
A loud voice from heaven speaking to the priests

6.question: What did the men of Beth-shemesh do when they saw the ark arrive?
options: They rejoiced and offered sacrifices
They fled in terror into their houses
They hid the ark inside an empty barn
They returned it to the priests of Shiloh

6.question: Why were many men of Beth-shemesh struck down?
options: For looking into the ark of the Lord
For touching the ark with their bare hands
For worshiping the gods of the Philistines
For disobeying Samuel's orders

7.title: Eben-ezer, the stone of help
7.text: Samuel set up a stone and called it Eben-ezer — 'stone of help' — saying, 'Hitherto hath the Lord helped us.'

7.question: What did Samuel ask Israel to do before the victory at Mizpah?
options: Put away the strange gods and serve the Lord only
Rebuild the altar destroyed by the Philistines at Shiloh
Offer daily sacrifices at the altar in the city of Gilgal
Pay an annual tribute of silver to the Philistines

7.question: How did the Lord defeat the Philistines at Mizpah?
options: He thundered upon them and discomfited them
He sent fire from heaven upon their camp
He opened the earth and swallowed their whole army
He sent an angel to destroy the camp

7.question: What name did Samuel give the stone he raised, saying 'Hitherto hath the Lord helped us'?
options: Eben-ezer
Beth-el
Gilgal
Shiloh

8.title: Rejecting the King of kings
8.text: When the people asked for a human king, the Lord told Samuel: 'they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.'

8.question: What did the elders of Israel ask of Samuel?
options: A king, like the other nations had
A high priest to judge all the people
A permanent army to fight against the Philistines
That Samuel judge them forever

8.question: What did Samuel warn about the king they asked for?
options: That he would take their sons, daughters, fields and goods
That he would reign only over the northern tribes of Israel
That he would never raise an army or build chariots of war
That he would be elected by the people in an assembly

8.question: According to Samuel, what else would the king take from the people?
options: A tenth of the harvests and flocks
The jewels and gold kept in their houses
The camels and horses used in warfare
The bronze tools of the farmers

8.question: How did the people respond to Samuel's warning?
options: They insisted: 'We will have a king over us'
They agreed: 'We will do whatever Samuel commands'
They replied: 'We will choose our own judge'
They stayed silent, without answering

9.title: Saul, the tallest
9.text: Saul is introduced as a handsome young man, taller than all the people from the shoulders up — and of the small tribe of Benjamin.

9.question: Why had Saul left home, on the occasion he met Samuel?
options: He was seeking his father's lost donkeys
He was delivering a gift to the priest of the city
He was fleeing the pursuit of the Philistines against his family
He was seeking a prophet to bless the harvest

9.question: Whom did Saul and his servant decide to consult about the donkeys?
options: The seer (the prophet Samuel)
The chief of all elders in the city
The keeper of the sanctuary at Shiloh
The captain of the guard

9.question: What was a prophet formerly called in Israel?
options: A seer
A judge
A Levite
An elder

9.question: What had the Lord revealed to Samuel the day before Saul came?
options: That he would send a man to be anointed captain of Israel
That Saul would be chosen to serve as priest in the temple
That a great famine would spread throughout the land of Israel soon
That the Philistines would soon attack the city of Shiloh

9.question: How did Saul respond to the honor Samuel gave him?
options: He said he was of Benjamin, the smallest tribe
He declared he was unworthy to be called captain
He said his family was the richest of all in Israel
He refused to accept any honor from the prophet

9.question: What did Samuel prepare to do with Saul at dawn?
options: Reveal to him the word of God and anoint him
Send him back to his father's house without an answer
Present him publicly to all the people as king
Offer him a sacrifice of thanksgiving

10.title: 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'
10.text: When Saul prophesied with a band of prophets, his acquaintances were amazed, and the saying arose: 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'

10.question: What did Samuel do to Saul privately?
options: He anointed him with oil as captain of Israel
He gave him a sword as a sign of the covenant
He clothed him with royal robes before the people
He blessed him as priest of the temple

10.question: What sign happened to Saul, becoming a saying in Israel?
options: He prophesied among the prophets
He healed the sick people in the city of Gilgal
He received power to defeat the Philistines alone
He spoke in strange tongues

10.question: What did Saul tell his uncle about the kingdom?
options: Nothing — he hid the matter of the kingdom
He told everything, including the secret anointing
He said Samuel had rejected him as king
He claimed he would be army general

10.question: How was Saul publicly chosen king at Mizpah?
options: By lot, tribe by tribe
By general acclamation of the people
By Samuel's direct appointment
By battle among the chiefs

10.question: Where was Saul found when he was to be presented as king?
options: Hidden among the baggage
Taking refuge in his uncle's house
Hidden behind the altar of the temple
Sleeping under a nearby tree

11.title: The Spirit moves a king
11.text: When the Spirit of God came upon Saul, his indignation gathered all Israel in a single day to relieve Jabesh-gilead.

11.question: What did Nahash the Ammonite demand of the men of Jabesh-gilead for a covenant?
options: To thrust out the right eye of each one
To hand over all the gold and silver of the city
To surrender and become slaves to the Ammonites
To swear eternal loyalty to Nahash

11.question: How did Saul gather Israel to relieve Jabesh?
options: The Spirit of God came on him and he summoned the people
He sent messengers to the Philistines asking for reinforcements
He gathered the elders of Israel to choose an experienced general
He consulted the priests and waited for signs in the sky

11.question: What happened after Saul defeated the Ammonites?
options: The kingdom was renewed and confirmed at Gilgal
Saul distributed the conquered lands to the people
The elders demanded that Samuel anoint another king
The people celebrated with sacrifices at Shiloh

12.title: Thunder in the harvest
12.text: Samuel called for thunder and rain in the time of wheat harvest — something unusual — as a sign that asking for a king had been a sin before God.

12.question: What did Samuel ask the people to witness about his leadership?
options: That he had never taken from or oppressed anyone
That he had always judged the people with partiality
That he had gathered riches at the people's expense
That he had named his sons as kings

12.question: What did Samuel recall to the people in his speech?
options: How God had delivered them since Egypt
The blessings promised to future kings
The names of all the priests of Israel
The laws given on Mount Sinai

12.question: What condition did Samuel set for the king and people to prosper?
options: To fear and obey the Lord
To offer daily sacrifices
To defeat all neighboring enemies
To keep the ark in the palace

12.question: What sign did God give through Samuel, in the time of wheat harvest?
options: Thunder and rain
An eclipse
Fire from heaven
An earthquake

12.question: What did Samuel promise to do, even after the sinful request for a king?
options: Not to cease praying for them and to teach them the good way
To gather a new council of elders to judge all the people
To withdraw to the desert and never speak to the people of Israel again
To secretly anoint a new king to replace Saul

13.title: 'A man after his own heart'
13.text: In rejecting Saul's disobedience, Samuel announces that God has sought 'a man after his own heart' to be prince — the first hint of David.

13.question: Who smote the garrison of the Philistines, sparking the conflict?
options: Jonathan
Saul
David
Samuel

13.question: What was happening while Saul waited for Samuel at Gilgal?
options: The people, afraid, began to scatter
Jonathan was secretly gathering troops at Michmash
The priests were preparing a new stone altar
Saul was gathering hidden weapons in the caves

13.question: What error did Saul commit before the battle?
options: He offered the burnt offering without waiting for Samuel
He dismissed the army before Samuel arrived at Gilgal for battle
He consulted the idols of the Philistines before deciding to attack
He divided the army into two groups without consulting the Lord

13.question: What did Samuel tell Saul because of his disobedience?
options: That his kingdom would not continue
That his sons would inherit the throne
That the Philistines would soon surrender
That he would lose all his goods

13.question: Why did Israel have almost no swords or spears?
options: The Philistines allowed no smiths in Israel
The Israelites had melted down all their weapons into idols
A fire had destroyed the weapons arsenal at Gilgal
Many of the warriors had fled to Judah

14.title: 'To save by many or by few'
14.text: Before attacking alone with his armourbearer, Jonathan declared: 'there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.'

14.question: Who went secretly to attack the Philistine garrison, with only his armourbearer?
options: Jonathan
Saul
David
Abner

14.question: What principle of faith did Jonathan declare before attacking?
options: It is not hard for the Lord to save by many or by few
That the whole army had to gather before attacking the Philistines
That the Lord would only save with a great multitude of warriors
That they should wait for reinforcements before acting

14.question: What sign did Jonathan set to know whether God would deliver them?
options: If the Philistines said 'come up to us'
If the Philistines threw torches into the air
If a cloud covered the sun during the morning
If they heard the sound of trumpets

14.question: What caused panic in the camp of the Philistines?
options: An earthquake sent by God
A cloud of smoke that blinded the army
A great wind that knocked down the Philistine tents
A surprise attack by the Hebrews

14.question: What rash oath did Saul impose on the army that day?
options: That no one eat until evening, until he was avenged
That no one touch the spoil before the victory was complete
That the entire army remain in fasting for three whole days
That no one touch the weapons of the enemies

14.question: What did Jonathan do, not knowing of his father's oath?
options: He ate a little honey and his strength returned
He refused to eat anything so as not to break the oath
He warned the people about the oath before they ate
He commanded that no one touch the honey

14.question: What sin did the famished people commit at evening?
options: They ate flesh with the blood
They stole food from the Philistines
They worshiped the gods of the Philistines
They fled from the battlefield

14.question: Why did God not answer Saul when he inquired that day?
options: Because of a sin committed in the camp
Because the priests had abandoned the camp
Because the people had offered an unclean sacrifice
Because Saul had not consulted Samuel

14.question: On whom did the lot fall, for breaking the oath unknowingly?
options: Jonathan
Saul
The armourbearer
Abner

14.question: What did the people do when Saul would have killed Jonathan over the oath?
options: They rescued him, for he had won the victory
They asked Saul to annul the oath immediately
They demanded Jonathan be exiled instead of killed
They remained silent before Saul's decision

15.title: The rejected king
15.text: After sparing Agag, Saul was finally rejected by God as king; Samuel mourned for him — and the way opened for David's anointing.

15.question: What command did the Lord give Saul through Samuel?
options: To utterly destroy the Amalekites
To make a peace treaty with the Amalekites
To spare the king and livestock for sacrifice
To conquer all the land of Canaan

15.question: How did Saul disobey the Lord?
options: He spared king Agag and the best of the livestock
He hid himself during the battle against the Amalekites
He made a secret alliance with the king of Amalek
He refused to fight against the Amalekites

15.question: What did the Lord say to Samuel about Saul?
options: That he repented of having made him king
That he would grant victory over all his enemies
That he would establish his throne forever in Israel
That he would send fire upon his army

15.question: What excuse did Saul give for the spared livestock?
options: That the people kept it to sacrifice to the Lord
That the Amalekites left it behind during the retreat
That Samuel had commanded him to spare it for the temple
That the soldiers insisted on keeping the cattle

15.question: What principle did Samuel declare to Saul?
options: 'To obey is better than sacrifice'
'The offering pleases more than obedience'
'The priest intercedes for the sinner'
'The king has absolute authority'

15.question: What did Samuel say would happen to Saul's kingdom?
options: It would be torn away and given to another better than he
It would be greatly strengthened and extended to all the tribes of Israel
It would pass down peacefully to his eldest son as an inheritance
It would be divided equally between his two tribes

15.question: What did Samuel do with Agag, king of the Amalekites?
options: He killed him before the Lord at Gilgal
He sent him back to Amalek unharmed and in peace
He made him a servant in the camp of Israel
He pardoned him before all the people

16.title: God looks on the heart
16.text: When Samuel was impressed by Jesse's eldest son's appearance, the Lord said: 'man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.'

16.question: Where did God send Samuel to anoint the new king?
options: To the house of Jesse, in Beth-lehem
To the camp of Israel, at Gilgal in the valley
To the tent of meeting, in the wilderness
To Mount Sinai, to worship the Lord

16.question: What did the Lord teach Samuel about choosing the king?
options: Man looks on appearance, but God looks on the heart
The king must be chosen for his strength and stature
God always chooses the eldest son of the whole family
The Lord always chooses strictly by royal lineage

16.question: Whom did Samuel anoint, the youngest son of Jesse?
options: David
Eliab
Abinadab
Shammah

16.question: What troubled Saul, leading him to seek a harp player?
options: An evil spirit
An eye disease
Old age
Famine

16.question: How did David enter Saul's service?
options: By playing the harp to relieve him
By serving as a messenger for King Saul
By fighting bravely against the Philistines
By defeating the giant Goliath in a duel

17.title: Five smooth stones
17.text: David refused Saul's armor and chose five smooth stones from the brook and his sling — a shepherd's weapons — trusting that the battle was the Lord's.

17.question: Who was the Philistine giant who defied the army of Israel?
options: Goliath
Nahash
Agag
Sisera

17.question: What did Goliath propose to the Israelites?
options: A duel: that they send one man to fight him
That Saul send his entire army to fight him
That ten Israelite warriors fight him at the same time
That the Israelites surrender all their land

17.question: Why did Jesse send David to the army's camp?
options: To bring food to his soldier brothers
To deliver a secret message to King Saul
To summon him to enlist in Saul's army
To receive direct orders from King Saul

17.question: For how many days did Goliath defy Israel, morning and evening?
options: Forty days
Seven days
Three days
A hundred days

17.question: What was promised to whoever defeated Goliath?
options: The king's daughter and great riches
A commanding position over all Israel's army
Gold, silver, and robes of honor from the king's house
Lands and flocks as a royal reward

17.question: How did David's eldest brother Eliab react to him in the camp?
options: He was angry and rebuked him
He laughed and completely ignored him
He praised his courage before everyone
He asked him to go back

17.question: What experience did David cite to Saul to show he could defeat Goliath?
options: Having killed a lion and a bear protecting the flock
Having single-handedly defeated a large band of raiders
Having received formal military training at the royal court
Having tended his father's flock since childhood

17.question: Why did David refuse Saul's armor?
options: He was not used to it; he chose the sling and five stones
It was too large and kept him from moving with full freedom
It had certainly been made for a much taller and stronger man
He had never worn bronze armor in any battle before

17.question: In whose name did David say he would face Goliath?
options: In the name of the Lord of hosts
In the name of King Saul and all Israel
In the name of his father Jesse and his tribe
In the name of the prophet Samuel

17.question: How did David bring down the giant Goliath?
options: With a stone from the sling, striking his forehead
With a strong sword strike to the giant's own head
With a spear thrust that pierced through his chest
With the giant's own sword, seized from him

17.question: What did the Philistines do when they saw their champion dead?
options: They fled, and Israel pursued them
They regrouped to fight another battle
They sent messengers asking for peace
They kept fighting even harder

17.question: What did Saul ask after David's victory?
options: Whose son David was
How old he was
Where he learned to fight
Whether he wanted to be king

18.title: David and Jonathan
18.text: 'The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.' Their friendship, sealed by a covenant, is one of the Bible's most famous — loyal even when it cost Jonathan the throne.

18.question: What did Jonathan do when he met David?
options: He made a covenant with him and loved him as himself
He publicly challenged him to a duel before the people
He accused him before Saul of treason against the kingdom
He grew suspicious of him and reported him to the king

18.question: What song of the women made Saul jealous of David?
options: 'Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands'
'The Lord exalted David above all the mighty captains of Israel'
'Blessed be the king who humbled the Philistines through David'
'David slew the giant and delivered Israel from bondage'

18.question: What did Saul try to do to David while he played the harp?
options: Pin him to the wall with a javelin
Arrest him and lock him in a dungeon
Banish him from the kingdom and seize his goods
Poison him with a bitter drink

18.question: Why did Saul offer his daughter in marriage to David?
options: Hoping the Philistines would kill him
To reward him for his bravery in battle
To make peace between their two families
By direct command of the prophet Samuel

18.question: What unusual price did Saul demand of David for marrying his daughter Michal?
options: A hundred Philistine foreskins
A hundred talents of pure silver
Two hundred fine horses for the army
Fifty head of choice cattle

18.question: Why did Saul fear David more and more?
options: Because the Lord was with David and he prospered
Because David had been anointed king before all the people of Israel
Because David had defeated the Philistine army all by himself
Because the people acclaimed David as the true king

19.title: David becomes a fugitive
19.text: Saul's envy turns into open persecution. From here on, David — already anointed but still without a throne — lives for years as a fugitive until Saul's death.

19.question: What did Jonathan do when Saul ordered David killed?
options: He interceded for him and reconciled them for a time
He agreed with his father and helped plan David's escape
He fled with David to Samuel's house in the city of Ramah
He warned the Philistines about Saul's plans

19.question: What did Saul try again against David with the javelin?
options: Pin him while he played the harp
Throw it at him during a royal feast
Drive it into the door of his own room
Give it as a gift to a trusted servant

19.question: Who helped David escape through a window at night?
options: Michal, his wife
Jonathan, his friend
Samuel, the prophet
Abner, the general

19.question: How did Michal deceive Saul's messengers seeking David?
options: She put an image in the bed, pretending he was sick
She locked the doors and told the messengers he had fled far away
She lied that he had died suddenly during the previous night
She dressed as David to fool the household guards

19.question: What happened to Saul when he went to Naioth after David?
options: The Spirit of God came on him and he prophesied
He fell ill and had to return without reaching David
He was captured by David's men and taken prisoner
He gave up and returned without finding anyone at Naioth

20.title: A covenant sealed by oath
20.text: Jonathan loved David 'as his own soul' and made with him an oath of loyalty between their houses — even knowing that David, not he, would be king.

20.question: What did David ask of Jonathan at the start of the chapter?
options: To find out whether Saul truly meant to kill him
To negotiate peace between himself and King Saul
To seek shelter with the priests at Nob for safety
To ask forgiveness from the prophet Samuel

20.question: What plan did they agree on to test Saul's intentions?
options: David would miss the new-moon feast
Jonathan would publicly announce that David had left
Saul would hold a private feast without David
David would go to Bethlehem with Jonathan

20.question: What covenant did Jonathan make with David?
options: Loyalty between their houses forever
To reign together dividing Israel's people into two parts
Permanent war against the house of Saul until death
Mutual protection only until the end of Saul's reign

20.question: What sign would Jonathan use to warn David of danger?
options: The direction of the arrows he would shoot
A wave of a white cloak signaled from the watchtower
A message delivered secretly by a trusted servant
A shout of warning from the city wall

20.question: What would serve as witness of the covenant between David and Jonathan?
options: The Lord, between them forever
A written oath before the priests
King Saul, as the official witness
An altar built nearby in the field

20.question: What did Saul ask on noticing David's absence at the feast?
options: Why the son of Jesse had not come
Whether anyone had seen David in the city
How many days David would remain hidden
Why Jonathan had arrived late

20.question: How did Saul react when Jonathan defended David?
options: He raged and threw the javelin at his own son
He ordered the guards to arrest David immediately
He tore off his own royal robe in furious silence
He crowned David there in front of everyone

20.question: How did Jonathan warn David of danger, as agreed?
options: By shooting arrows beyond the boy who fetched them
By waving a white cloth from the top of the city wall
By sending a servant quietly with a secret message
By blowing the trumpet three times at dawn

20.question: How did David and Jonathan part?
options: They wept and renewed their oath of friendship
They exchanged gifts and promised to meet again
They went together to speak with Saul about peace
They agreed to meet again soon in secret

21.title: The holy bread
21.text: The showbread could be eaten only by the priests; Jesus cited this episode of David to teach that mercy is above the letter of the law.

21.question: What did the priest Ahimelech give David at Nob?
options: The holy bread and Goliath's sword
Gold and silver kept in the temple treasury
A horse and a full set of battle armor
An army ready for the battle

21.question: Who was at Nob and would later inform on the priests to Saul?
options: Doeg the Edomite
Abiathar the Levite
Abner the general
Jonathan the son

21.question: What did David do when he found himself in danger before Achish, king of Gath?
options: He feigned madness to escape
He confronted Achish in direct combat
He asked the king's servants for help
He promised to serve as a soldier

22.title: The band of Adullam
22.text: At the cave of Adullam the distressed, the indebted and the discontented gathered to David — about 400 men, the core of his future army.

22.question: Who gathered to David at the cave of Adullam?
options: His family and about 400 men in distress
All the elders of Israel and their armed servants
An army sent by the king of Moab to assist him
Three hundred men chosen by Jonathan

22.question: Who told Saul that the priest Ahimelech had helped David?
options: Doeg the Edomite
Ahiah, the shepherd of Saul
Zebadiah, captain of Gibeah
Abner, cousin of Saul

22.question: Of what did Saul accuse the priest Ahimelech?
options: Of conspiring with David against him
Of giving temple weapons to the Philistines
Of hiding David at Nob without telling the king
Of betraying the whole house of Saul

22.question: What did Saul's guards refuse to do?
options: Kill the priests of the Lord
Deliver David into Saul's hands
Chase David to the wilderness of Ziph
Burn down the city of Nob

22.question: Who escaped the massacre at Nob and fled to David?
options: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech
Jonathan, the very son of Saul
Samuel, the elderly prophet of Ramah
Michal, the wife of David

23.title: Always inquiring of the Lord
23.text: Unlike Saul, David asks the Lord before each step, by means of the ephod brought by Abiathar — and is guided in every decision.

23.question: What did David do for the city of Keilah?
options: He saved it from a Philistine attack
He conquered it and gave it to the king of Moab
He fortified its walls against Saul's army
He demanded tribute from its people

23.question: How did David inquire of the Lord about what to do?
options: By the ephod, with the priest Abiathar
By sending secret messengers to Jerusalem
Through dreams sent to him during the night
By casting lots with sacred stones

23.question: What did the Lord reveal to David about the men of Keilah?
options: That they would deliver him into Saul's hand
That they would rise up against Saul for him
That they would send immediate help for his escape
That they would crown him as new king

23.question: What did Jonathan do when he found David in the wilderness?
options: He strengthened him in God and renewed the covenant
He convinced him to fully surrender to King Saul
He led him straight back to Saul's own camp
He asked David to give him half the kingdom

23.question: Who betrayed David's hiding place, telling Saul?
options: The Ziphites
The Philistines
The men of Keilah
The Edomites

23.question: What saved David when Saul had nearly surrounded him in the wilderness?
options: News of a Philistine raid called Saul back
A secret messenger from Jonathan warned David just in time
David's own soldiers completely surrounded Saul's army
A fierce storm halted the whole army's advance

24.title: Respect for the anointed
24.text: Though he could have killed Saul, David did not raise his hand against 'the Lord's anointed' — he chose to wait on God's timing rather than seize the throne by force.

24.question: Where did Saul enter, not knowing David was hiding there?
options: A cave where David was concealed
In a sheepfold beside the path through the mountains
In the camp of his three thousand chosen men
On the cliffs of the wild goats, in the open

24.question: What did David do instead of killing Saul in the cave?
options: He cut off only the edge of his robe
He bound him and left him trapped at the cave's entrance
He took his sword and hid it beneath his robe
He lightly wounded his arm with his own sword

24.question: Why did David's heart smite him even for cutting the robe?
options: For touching the Lord's anointed
For having disobeyed a commandment of God
For having broken an oath sworn to Saul
For having acted with great recklessness

24.question: How did David prove to Saul he did not want to kill him?
options: He showed him the piece of robe he had cut
He freed all the prisoners he had captured
He brought witnesses who confirmed his innocence
He swore before all the people of Israel

24.question: How did Saul react to David's act in the cave?
options: He wept and admitted David was more righteous than he
He ordered his men to pursue David even more fiercely
He demanded that David return the torn piece at once
He denied that David had cut off his robe

25.title: Nabal, the 'fool'
25.text: The name 'Nabal' means 'fool' or 'senseless.' His rudeness nearly causes a massacre — averted by the wisdom of his wife Abigail.

25.question: How are Nabal and his wife Abigail described?
options: Nabal churlish and foolish; Abigail prudent and beautiful
Nabal generous and exceedingly wise; Abigail proud and foolish
Nabal righteous and brave; Abigail foolish and dishonorable
Both were known as humble and peaceable shepherds

25.question: What did Nabal do when David's men asked for provisions?
options: He refused with scorn
He gave them double
He invited them to a feast
He fled

25.question: What did David prepare to do against Nabal?
options: Attack him with his armed men
Send messengers demanding payment
Seize his flocks without violence
Wait for Nabal to repent

25.question: What did Abigail do on learning of the danger?
options: She took food and went to meet David to appease him
She warned Nabal to flee with his whole household and goods
She hid inside her tent so that no one could find her
She called the Philistines to attack David's camp

25.question: What did Abigail ask of David?
options: That he not shed blood in personal revenge
That he take personal revenge with his own hands
That he punish Nabal openly before all his servants
That he renounce his sword in favor of Saul

25.question: How did David respond to Abigail's counsel?
options: He praised God and gave up the revenge
He refused the gift and attacked the camp
He demanded that Nabal kneel down before him
He demanded double what had been offered

25.question: What happened when Abigail told Nabal what she had done?
options: His heart failed and became as a stone
He drove her out of the house in great anger
He gathered his servants together to defend himself
He laughed and called his servants to feast

25.question: What happened to Nabal about ten days later?
options: The Lord smote him and he died
He recovered and lived ten more years
He fled to Gath and hid there quickly
He reconciled with David

25.question: What did David do after Nabal's death?
options: He took Abigail as his wife
He distributed his goods to the poor
He returned everything to Nabal's family
He married another widow

26.title: Sparing Saul again
26.text: A second time David spares Saul's life, telling Abishai: 'stretch not forth thine hand against the Lord's anointed.' He trusts that God, in due time, will set things right.

26.question: What did David and Abishai do in Saul's camp by night?
options: They went in while everyone slept
They surrounded the tent and seized Abner
They killed the guards and fled quickly
They swapped the army's weapons

26.question: What did David answer when Abishai wanted to kill Saul on the spot?
options: 'Stretch not forth thine hand against the Lord's anointed'
'Take his crown and his sword as the spoils of this battle'
'Let Abishai strike him down now with his very own spear'
'Call Joab so that he may decide this matter now'

26.question: What did David take from Saul's camp as proof?
options: Saul's spear and water cruse
The royal crown and scepter from the camp
Abner's sword and bronze shield
The king's signet ring, kept safe

26.question: How did David show Saul he could have killed him?
options: He called out from afar, showing the spear and water he had taken
He sent Abishai back carrying the empty water jug as a sign of mercy
He had Joab publicly hand over the spear before the whole camp at dawn
He left a written message inside Saul's own royal tent

26.question: How did Saul respond this second time?
options: He admitted his sin and blessed David
He ordered Abner to pursue David once more
He promised a reward to whoever captured David
He demanded David return to the palace

27.title: Ziklag, David's town
27.text: Achish gave Ziklag to David; the town belonged to the kings of Judah from then on. There David built up his forces, while pretending to be a Philistine ally.

27.question: Where did David go to live, to escape Saul for good?
options: To the land of the Philistines, with Achish of Gath
To the land of the Amalekites, to live in peace
To the city of Hebron, to gather an army
To the wilderness of Ziph, to hide

27.question: What town did Achish give David to dwell in?
options: Ziklag
Gath
Hebron
Adullam

28.title: The king who sought what he had banned
28.text: Saul himself had driven the mediums and wizards out of Israel, as the Law commands; but in desperation he turned to a medium at En-dor.

28.question: What had Saul done before, yet now sought in desperation?
options: He had banished mediums, but now sought one
He had rebuilt the altar, but now abandoned it
He had sworn to obey God, but now disobeyed again
He had consulted the priests, but now ignored them

28.question: Why did Saul turn to a medium at En-dor?
options: Because the Lord no longer answered him
Because he feared facing the Philistines alone
Because Samuel had appeared to him in a dream before
Because he wanted to test his servants

28.question: Whom did Saul ask the medium of En-dor to bring up?
options: Samuel
David
Eli
Jonathan

28.question: What message did 'Samuel' give Saul that night?
options: That the kingdom was given to David and he would die the next day
That the Philistines would be defeated and David crowned very soon
That God would forgive his sin if he repented right there that night
That the Amalekites would be spared once more this very time

28.question: What happened to Saul after hearing the prophecy?
options: He fell to the ground, strengthless, and was fed
He rose up furious and attacked the medium without mercy
He wept bitterly and ran back to the camp at once
He fell deeply asleep inside the medium's tent

29.title: Spared an impossible war
29.text: By being sent back, David was spared an impossible situation: having to fight alongside the Philistines against his own people, Israel.

29.question: Why did the Philistine lords not want David in the battle?
options: They feared he would turn against them in the fight
They thought he would bring bad luck to the Philistine army
They wanted to keep him to guard the borders of Gath
He had refused to fight against Israel

29.question: What did Achish order David before the battle at Gilboa?
options: To go back, so as not to fight against Israel
To lead the rearguard until the end of the battle
To hand over his weapons before leaving the camp
To swear loyalty to Achish in public

30.title: 'David encouraged himself in the Lord'
30.text: When the embittered people spoke of stoning him, 'David encouraged himself in the Lord his God' (v6) — a much-cited verse about trusting God in crisis.

30.question: What did David find when he returned to Ziklag?
options: The city burned and the families carried off captive by the Amalekites
An enemy army of Philistines camped among the ruins awaiting his return
Saul and his men waiting there to hold him responsible for losing the city
The city intact, with all its residents safe and untouched

30.question: What did David do when the embittered people spoke of stoning him?
options: He encouraged himself in the Lord and inquired of God
He fled alone into the distant mountains seeking refuge and safety
He surrendered command to his own men and gave it up entirely
He attacked his own people out of sheer despair

30.question: Who helped David find the Amalekites who had raided Ziklag?
options: An Egyptian servant abandoned by the raiders
A messenger sent by the elders of Judah to warn him
A prophet who received revelation about their whereabouts
A Philistine scout captured along the way

30.question: How much did David recover from the Amalekites?
options: Everything — nothing was missing, neither people nor goods
Only half of the captured people and none of the plundered goods
Only the flocks, but none of the families that were carried away
Only the young children and the elderly people

30.question: What rule did David set about dividing the spoil?
options: An equal share for those who stayed with the baggage and those who fought
A larger share for the commanders and the rest divided among the other soldiers
Everything reserved only for those who fought directly in the battle itself
No share at all for those who stayed behind guarding the baggage

30.question: With whom did David share the spoil, winning their friendship?
options: The elders of Judah
The Philistines
The remaining Amalekites
The priests of Nob

31.title: Jabesh-gilead repays the kindness
31.text: The men of Jabesh-gilead recovered the bodies of Saul and his sons — repaying the rescue Saul had given them at the start of his reign (chapter 11).

31.question: What happened to Jonathan and Saul's sons in the battle at mount Gilboa?
options: They were slain by the Philistines
They fled to the neighboring mountains
They were taken prisoner by the Philistines
They surrendered without a fight

31.question: How did Saul die, so as not to fall alive into Philistine hands?
options: He fell upon his own sword
He was killed in battle by the Philistine archers
He fled wounded and died of his wounds days later
He was captured and killed by the Philistines

31.question: Who recovered the bodies of Saul and his sons and buried them with honor?
options: The men of Jabesh-gilead
The priests of Shiloh, in a solemn procession
The elders of Israel gathered in assembly
The servants of king Achish
